title: Orientation engineering is a universal strategy for ferroelectric trans-switching
abstract: About two decades ago, ``strain engineering'' emerged as a powerful strategy to tune epitaxial thin films. Here we contend that ''orientation engineering'' - that is, controlling the film's growth direction - constitutes a complementary design route that opens unprecedented opportunities and deserves greater attention. Specifically, we show that orientation engineering can endow standard ferroelectric compounds with exotic and useful behaviors that may be difficult or impossible to obtain otherwise. Critically, we predict it readily enables ''trans-switching,'' where polarization components switch perpendicularly to the applied electric field, paving the way for novel 3D device architectures. We also show that, by controlling the electric screening provided by electrodes in contact with the film, ferrielectric behavior can be obtained. Notably, one can even design an operational mode where the switching is, in effect, fully transversal to the applied field. Supported by phenomenological calculations for representative compounds LiNbO$_3$ and BaTiO$_3$, we thus propose orientation engineering as a powerful and general method to unlock unprecedented functionalities in common ferroelectrics.
summary: This work proposes 'orientation engineering' as a powerful, general design strategy for ferroelectric materials, showing it can induce 'trans-switching'—where polarization switches perpendicular to the applied field. By analyzing the free energy landscape based on the film's growth direction, the authors predict novel functionalities in common ferroelectrics, opening pathways for advanced 3D device architectures.
main_problem: To demonstrate that controlling the growth direction ('orientation engineering') in ferroelectric thin films is a universal method to induce exotic switching behaviors, particularly 'trans-switching'.
main_result: Orientation engineering enables trans-switching, where polarization components switch perpendicularly to the applied electric field, in common ferroelectrics like LiNbO3 and BaTiO3.
method: Theoretical analysis using Landau theory, symmetry arguments, and phenomenological calculations applied to representative ferroelectric compounds.
model_or_system: The study focuses on epitaxial ferroelectric thin films, modeled using a fourth-order Landau free energy functional that is adapted based on the angle ($	heta$) between the principal axis and the growth direction.
key_observables: Hysteresis loops, off-diagonal dielectric susceptibility ($\epsilon_0\chi_{\perp,\parallel}$), and the polarization components ($P_{\parallel}$, $P_{\perp}$).
important_parameters: Growth angle ($	heta$), electric screening parameter ($\lambda$), and temperature ($T$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on symmetry-driven effects and assumes the validity of the Landau theory framework for describing the phase transitions.

Figures illustrate the energy landscapes and hysteresis loops for LiNbO3 and BaTiO3, contrasting standard switching ($	heta=0^\circ$) with trans-switching observed at oblique angles ($	heta

paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the concept of orientation engineering as a superior design route compared to strain engineering, deriving the relevant free energy terms, and then applying this framework to analyze both uniaxial (LiNbO3) and triaxial (BaTiO3) ferroelectrics under varying screening conditions.
why_interesting: While focused on ferroelectrics, the concept of controlling symmetry breaking via geometric orientation ($	heta$) to induce novel coupling terms ($f P_\parallel P_\perp$) is analogous to engineering coupling terms in quantum Hamiltonians to achieve desired non-local or perpendicular dynamics.

A principal direction of the crystalline lattice (ˆz) forms an angle (θ) with the vertical growth direc- tion. For arbitrary θ, the polarization (P) can be projected onto both out-of-plane (P∥) and in-plane (P⊥) components. Improper-like couplings between P∥and P⊥naturally occur for θ ̸= 0, leading to trans-switching.

FIG. 4. Effect of screening on tetragonal BaTiO3 at 300 K with θ = 10◦orientation. Panel a) shows trans-switching for perfect short circuit boundary conditions (λ = 0), as the vertical field E∥connects the two free-energy minima with maximum |P∥| in panel b). Increasing λ in Panels c) and d) removes these minima at zero field field (although they can still be induced by a finite E∥), so the remanent equilibrium states display large P⊥and a relatively small P∥. This results in a triple hysteresis loop. Further increasing λ removes the remanent P∥almost completely, leading to a situation with a nearly purely linear dielectric response for P∥, and (trans-)switching restricted to P⊥.
